title: Terminal Portfolio Updates
content: # Terminal Portfolio Update [MIR_OS]:
- TYPE: System Architecture & Feature Release
- TARGET: Terminal Portfolio (MIR_OS V0.0.5)
- COMPONENT: VFS, CI/CD, Text Editing
- STATUS: Deployed
# THE_OBJECTIVE

Today’s goal was twofold: transform the terminal from a static read-only interface into a fully interactive operating system, and build a "hands-off" CI/CD pipeline so I can publish blog posts directly from a separate GitHub repository without touching the core React code.
# THE_EXECUTION
I successfully engineered and deployed several major system protocols:

* [VIM_EDITOR]: Integrated a functional Vim-like text editor. Users can now create, edit, and save files directly into the terminal's Session RAM using authentic Vim commands (`:i`, `[ESC]`, `:wq`, `:q`).
* [FILE_MANAGEMENT]: Implemented the `rm` command. Users can delete their own session files, but the system actively guards against the deletion of core portfolio metadata (Permission Denied).
* [SYSTEM_MANUAL]: Added a comprehensive `help` command, featuring a visually distinct UI and a Vim Quickstart guide for recruiters unfamiliar with Linux environments.
* [DYNAMIC_VFS]: Built an "LOG BLOG" that dynamically mounts external JSON data into the Virtual File System on boot, allowing commands like `cd` and `ls` to instantly recognize new directories.
# THE_ROADBLOCK
Automating the blog sync was a multi-layered debugging session across three environments (Local Windows, GitHub Actions, and Vercel).

Vercel's strict TypeScript compiler blocked deployments due to unused function parameters. Meanwhile, the Python build script crashed because Windows PowerShell injected hidden UTF-16 Byte Order Marks (BOM) into my `.md` files. Finally, dynamically created folders threw "No such directory" errors because the terminal's input parser was aggressively lowercasing the user's input, causing case-sensitive mismatches in the Virtual File System.
# THE_RESOLUTION
* Silenced Vercel's strict TS errors using the underscore prefix standard (`_args`).
* Rewrote the Python file reader to fallback seamlessly between `utf-8-sig` and `utf-16`, using Regex to handle varying filename formats.
* Refactored the VFS to automatically convert all generated folders to lowercase, creating a foolproof navigation experience.
* Upgraded the `ls` command to contextually switch to a vertical layout when viewing blog directories to handle long filenames cleanly.
# NEXT_STEPS
The systems seems to be stable now. Next I would like to maybe add a theme changer as the green might not be for everyone.
